D.t: Xavier Becerra leads by 23.8 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 3,213,635 votes; a one point swing is about 67,485 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +17.3 and D +30.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +20.1. Your best recent poll is Emerson College at D +27.7; your worst is David Wolfson for Hilton (R) at D +9.1. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Los Angeles, a projected net 1,268,852 votes; Alameda, a projected net 369,460 votes; Santa Clara, a projected net 293,076 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Orange, D +0.7, 8.7% of the vote; Riverside, D +4.2, 5.7% of the vote; San Bernardino, D +2.3, 4.6% of the vote; Fresno, R +5.6, 2.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Xavier Becerra runs furthest behind in Placer, Orange, Kern. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 56% of voters, 53 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.79 points; Voters without a degree, 54% of voters, 62 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.69 points; Men, 49% of voters, 57 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.44 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Xavier Becerra: Immigration voters 29 to 70, Voters who can afford daily costs 52 to 48, White voters 53 to 46. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.2M cash against $2.1M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Money: Raised $21.4M against $29.7M for Xavier Becerra.
